fix: Every pointer move runs this block. `callbacks` is pushed on each accepted move (line 1117), so a drag allocates on every event; `accepts`, `rejects` and `scale_updates` do the same when used. Keep reusable scratch buffers on the input state (for example a `DispatchScratch { accepts, rejects, callbacks, scale_updates }` field on the tree's input struct). At the top take them with `let mut scratch = std::mem::take(&mut self.input.dispatch_scratch);`, call `clear()` on each, and put them back with `self.input.dispatch_scratch = scratch;` before returning. Taking the buffers out avoids borrow conflicts with the `self.input` borrows in the loop.

`GestureArena::entries` (crates/incular-gestures/src/arena.rs:157) returns an owned `Vec<GestureArenaEntry>`, so each pointer move allocates at line 1101 and again at line 1227 (line 1250 too for yields_taps streams). Change it to return a borrowed slice, `pub fn entries(&self, key: GestureArenaKey) -> &[GestureArenaEntry]`, if the per-key storage is a Vec. Then line 1101 borrows `self.input.gesture_arena` as a disjoint field and line 1227 needs no allocation. Update the callers of `entries` in the same change, and note the API change in the CHANGELOG under incular-gestures.

`scroll_drag_callbacks` runs on every press that starts a scroll drag and makes about six separate `Rc::new(Cell..)` allocations (lines 309, 310, 367, 296-297 from the caller at 960-963, and the clones for each closure). Put the per-drag cells in one struct held by one Rc, for example `struct DragCells { offset_since_last_stop: Cell<Option<f32>>, last_non_stationary: Cell<Option<Instant>>, remainder: Cell<f32>, carried_velocity: Cell<Option<f32>>, end_velocity: Cell<Option<f32>> }` with `let cells = Rc::new(DragCells { .. });`, and have each closure capture a clone of `cells`. This makes one allocation per press instead of about six.

Replace the attribute at line 697 with `#[expect(clippy::too_many_arguments, reason = "the pointer sample carries device, kind, buttons, sample and hit alongside the event")]`. Make the same change at line 718 on `dispatch_pointer_gesture_with_target`. Both functions take 8 parameters including self, so the lint fires and the expectation holds.
